chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The people say that shaving the head is a mutilation.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is an Umrah for us and a mutilation for our enemies.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shaving the head during Haj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reframes the physical act of shaving the head during Hajj not as a loss or mutilation, but as a distinct sign of devotion that distinguishes the faithful from their adversaries. This response highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the symbolic value of ritual acts, where external practices serve as markers of identity and spiritual purity, countering the superficial judgments of those outside the true path. The narration underscores the concept of *muthlah* (mutilation) as a relative term, dependent on the perspective of the observer and the intention behind the act.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the people are saying that shaving-off the head is a mutilation. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is an Umrah for us<sup>asws</sup> and a mutilation for our<sup>asws</sup> enemies’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from in a marfu‘ manner the following: “

I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘People say shaving of the head is like causing deformity.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is like performing al-‘Umrah for us and deformity for our enemies.’”
